about.text_short: Data Scientist & AI Engineer with a background in molecular biology and biomedical research (CBM-CSIC, Universität Konstanz). I apply scientific rigor, Machine Learning and generative AI to problems in Pharma, Health and Life Sciences, and I can take a solution all the way to production, as with Sextant IA.

experience_section.title: Experience
experience_section.intro: My career was shaped in institutional biomedical research, working with real, imperfect and valuable genomic data and treating it with the rigor science demands. Today I bring that same rigor to Data Science and AI: I currently train LLMs on data and bioinformatics problems.

items.story: I work freelance on a confidential project training large language models (LLMs) in Data Science and bioinformatics. I bring expert judgement: the same rigor I applied in the lab, now in service of AI.
impact: Training and evaluating LLMs in Data Science and bioinformatics.
Scientific judgement to ensure correct, verifiable and reproducible answers.

items.company: Severo Ochoa Centre for Molecular Biology (CBM-CSIC-UAM)
items.story: Here I took over the lab's computational strategy. I designed reproducible Python and Bash pipelines for more than 1 TB of genomic data, and learned that leading also means teaching: I guided 8 junior researchers through their first steps. When a Nanopore dataset was degraded by a hardware failure, I did not give it up for lost: I designed a hybrid strategy with Illumina that saved the project.
impact: Mentored 8 junior researchers (BSc, MSc and technicians).
Significantly reduced computing times through parallelisation with GNU Parallel.
Rescued a high-cost genomic dataset (ONT + Illumina).

items.story: Moving to Germany was both a professional and a personal leap. I owned the full data lifecycle: from experimental design and bioreactors to statistical analysis on HPC clusters. It was the first time data volume forced me to think like an engineer, and I discovered I loved it.
impact: De novo assembly of eukaryotic transcriptomes from environmental samples.
Multivariate analysis of communities in oligotrophic ecosystems.

other_items.story: Before building with AI, I wanted to understand how it is evaluated from the inside. I produced strict ground truth for search and computer vision algorithms, helping fine-tune models through RLHF. I found that my scientific training fitted naturally: evaluating a model is, at heart, designing a good experiment.
impact: Quality assurance for predictive and recommendation models.
Thorough analytical documentation for continuous accuracy improvement.

experience_section.lead: I did not come to data because it was trendy: I came because, as a scientist, I needed better tools to find answers.

projects_section.title: Projects
projects_section.intro: Every project started with a concrete problem. First, data analysis applied to biomedical problems; then, the ability to take an AI solution all the way to production.

items.title: Leishmania genome re-annotation with Ribo-Seq
items.challenge: A high-cost Nanopore sequencing experiment was degraded by a hardware failure, putting the redefinition of Leishmania donovani genome annotations at risk.
items.approach: I designed a hybrid strategy using high-fidelity Illumina reads to correct the transcriptome, with scripts parallelised via GNU Parallel to analyse Ribo-Seq data.
items.result: Project saved and published in Genes (2023), DOI 10.3390/genes14081637.

items.title: Sextant IA
items.challenge: Planning a tailor-made trip takes hours of scattered research and rarely includes the historical or cultural context that gives each place its meaning.
items.approach: I designed a backend that orchestrates LLMs to generate a main itinerary, break it down into daily plans and enrich it with cultural information, all served from a Django frontend.
items.result: A public production website with HTTPS and continuous deployment: a real product built and operated end to end.
items.story: Sextant IA was born from two passions: travelling and discovering the history of every place. I set out to build an assistant that does not just list destinations, but understands each traveller's preferences and designs a meaningful trip. I owned the project end to end: architecture, LLM-orchestrated backend, Django frontend, deployment and release to production.
items.production_note: The Sextant IA website is built, published and running in production. It is my clearest proof that I can take an idea from concept to a real product in users' hands.
impact: An engine that turns user preferences into a complete itinerary and dynamically breaks it down into daily plans.
Automatic enrichment with cultural and historical context for every location.
Continuous deployment: Oracle Cloud server with Nginx as a reverse proxy and HTTPS; every change to the Git main branch is released to production automatically.

items.title: Proteogenomics of Leishmania donovani
items.challenge: The Leishmania donovani reference genome did not capture every protein the parasite actually produces.
items.approach: I integrated mass spectrometry data with genome annotations and statistically validated the candidate coding sequences.
items.result: Identification of previously unannotated proteins, published in Genes (2024), DOI 10.3390/genes15060775.

items.title: DSMarket: Retail Forecasting
items.challenge: A retailer with more than 3,000 products needed to anticipate demand and understand its customers to optimise inventory.
items.approach: I cleaned 5 years of transactions (500K+ records), segmented customers with K-Means and trained Lasso Regression models for forecasting.
items.result: 6 actionable customer segments and an executive Power BI dashboard for inventory decisions.

items.title: This portfolio: AI-assisted website with continuous deployment
items.challenge: I wanted a portfolio that was not a static CV: multilingual, with an assistant able to answer questions about my career, and updating itself.
items.approach: I built it with Streamlit and a Google Gemini chatbot that answers from my own knowledge base. It is hosted on a Linux server on Oracle Cloud and deployed by a GitHub Actions pipeline that, on every push, updates the code and dependencies and restarts the service.
items.result: A production website in three languages, continuously deployed with no manual steps.

items.title: Environmental transcriptomics in aquatic ecosystems
items.challenge: Analysing microbial communities in nutrient-poor lakes produced data volumes impossible to process locally.
items.approach: I set up hybrid local/HPC workflows with Slurm to assemble transcriptomes de novo and applied multivariate statistics.
items.result: Efficient use of limited computing resources and robust community analysis.

items.title: Urban parking assistant (Hackathon)
items.type: Automation & Chatbots · 2nd Prize, No-Code Automation Hackathon Madrid
items.challenge: Finding legal parking in Madrid means cross-checking each zone's rules, the vehicle's environmental label and its real-time location.
items.approach: Over one weekend, as a team, we built a conversational assistant with Make and Woztell that cross-references licence plate, environmental label and GPS location through API integrations.
items.result: 2nd prize at the No-Code Automation Hackathon Madrid (Woztell & Make), with a working prototype that guides drivers to the nearest legal car park.
